title: Train tickets and hybrid cars: understanding spending habits
meta_description: An article exploring trends in train ticket sales and second-hand car sales using new data

breadcrumb.text: Train tickets and hybrid cars: understanding spending habits

lede: New data shows the effect of strikes on train ticket sales, and the most popular second-hand cars in Great Britain

body.text: 6 August 2024
From scanners at supermarket tills to ticket offices at railway stations, new data on everyday costs are improving our understanding of how prices are changing over time.
It is crucial to measure price changes as precisely as possible, because accurate measures of inflation are playing an increasingly vital role in business, government, and everyday life.
We are working with several new data sources to produce improved and more detailed inflation data. These include:
Transactional data on rail fares from Rail Delivery Group.
Web-provided data on second-hand cars from [Auto Trader](https://www.autotrader.co.uk/)
Microdata level rental data
Grocery retail scanner data

Data from these sources (including [40 million monthly rail fares](/economy/inflationandpriceindices/articles/usingtransactionlevelrailfaresdatatotransformconsumerpricestatisticsuk/2022-06-28) transactions from Rail Delivery Group and 300,000 monthly second-hand car sales from Auto Trader) have already improved our [Consumer price statistics.](/economy/inflationandpriceindices/bulletins/consumerpriceinflation/latest)

We have been working with several grocery retailers to gather scanner data, covering approximately 50% of the UK grocery market share. We hope to introduce this to our Consumer price statistics from March 2025.

Meanwhile, our [transformed private rental data](/economy/inflationandpriceindices/bulletins/privaterentandhousepricesuk/latest) provide greater detail in rental statistics and are more responsive to market changes.
As well as providing information on prices, these alternative data sources contain a wealth of other insights, including expenditure data.

body.h2: Sales of second-hand hybrid cars are on the rise
body.text: Sales of second-hand hybrid cars are on the rise

body.h2: Sales of second-hand hybrid cars are on the rise
body.text: Second-hand sales data from Auto Trader provide information on an estimated 300,000 used car sales per month, dating back to 2018.

body.h2: Sales of second-hand hybrid cars are on the rise
body.text: We use this to produce our petrol and diesel second-hand car inflation indices. As well as the advertised price, they include information on vehicle manufacturer, colour and fuel type.

body.h2: Sales of second-hand hybrid cars are on the rise
body.text: We estimate that the number of second-hand hybrid cars sold increased by 59% from 2022 to 2023.

body.h2: Sales of second-hand hybrid cars are on the rise
body.text: The additional detail in this data helps us assess how representative the [consumer price basket](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/articles/ukconsumerpriceinflationbasketofgoodsandservices/latest) is of the wider market. The “shopping basket” of items used to measure consumer price inflation changes each year to reflect consumer spending patterns.

body.h2: Sales of second-hand hybrid cars are on the rise
body.text: While the price of new hybrid and electric vehicles are included in the consumer price basket, second-hand sales of these cars are not captured because of the relatively low amount of money currently spent on them.

body.h2: Sales of second-hand hybrid cars are on the rise
body.text: Most hybrid and electric cars in the UK are bought new, meaning there are relatively low numbers of second-hand sales, but these new data allow us to monitor trends and update our representative basket when spending hits the necessary threshold.

body.h2: Sales of second-hand hybrid cars are on the rise
body.text: As the data are received daily, and a vehicle is listed for an average of 40 days before being sold, this still leaves multiple listings for each unique vehicle within the dataset.

body.h2: Sales of second-hand hybrid cars are on the rise
body.text: To estimate the number of individual cars we use a four-day gap before considering a listing "sold" to produce our index. For more information see our [Using Auto Trader car listings data to transform consumer price statistics, UK](/economy/inflationandpriceindices/articles/usingautotradercarlistingsdatatotransformconsumerpricestatisticsuk/2022-06-28) release.

body.h2: Sales of second-hand hybrid cars are on the rise
body.text: As these data are for advertised listings, they do not contain explicit sales revenue information.

body.text: ‘Newer’ is not always better when buying a second-hand car

body.h2: ‘Newer’ is not always better when buying a second-hand car
body.text: The biggest appeal when buying a second-hand car is usually the cost. They are typically cheaper than a new model, but the trade-off is that the older a car gets, the more likely it is to have problems later on.

body.h2: Making future improvements to our price statistics
body.text: Making future improvements to our price statistics

body.h2: Making future improvements to our price statistics
body.text: It is crucial for us to be able to continue improving our statistics, and using more detailed and accurate data helps us to achieve that.

body.h2: Making future improvements to our price statistics
body.text: We plan to update our headline statistics to include grocery scanner data in March 2025, allowing us to measure changes in food and drink prices more effectively.

body.h2: Making future improvements to our price statistics
body.text: As we continue to work with new, more robust data sources, we will be able to keep improving our statistics and find exciting ways to explore new trends.
